problems.problem: Source cutout edge remnants retained on silhouette
problems.evidence: Image 5 and baseline label/neck crops show a yellow-orange blob left of the label and ragged alpha jaggies along the left neck edge
problems.root_cause: Original matting artefacts baked into the transparent source asset, carried through compositing
problems.repair: Clean the alpha matte border (defringe/choke 1-2 px) while preserving genuine glass transmission

problems.problem: Contact shadow is a small dark nub rather than a shaped soft shadow
problems.evidence: Image 6 baseline contact crop: isolated dark bump under the green base, cloth texture uninterrupted beside it
problems.root_cause: Hand-painted contact dab in the original compositor instead of a light-consistent occlusion gradient
problems.repair: Replace with a broad, low-opacity elliptical occlusion gradient matched to diffuse frontal light

problems.problem: Base green reads over-bright versus baseline and source
problems.evidence: Image 6 row A contact crop: neon-green base band brighter than baseline and image 5
problems.root_cause: Linear-light RGBA compose without display-referred trim saturates the thin transmissive green glass
problems.repair: Apply a gentle tone-map/trim on the alpha-weighted green channel after linear compose

problems.problem: Label sits with a slight rotational skew
problems.evidence: Image 6 row A label crop: label top edge tilts relative to canvas horizontals, unlike baseline
problems.root_cause: Placement transform includes a residual rotation in the candidate compositor
problems.repair: Re-place product with identity rotation, verify label horizontals against canvas

problems.evidence: Image 6 row A contact crop: dark contact nub thinner and lighter than baseline row
problems.root_cause: Soft-shadow opacity reduced during linear-light pass
problems.repair: Restore occlusion density to at least baseline level

problems.problem: Source edge remnants persist (yellow blob left of label, neck jaggies)
problems.evidence: Image 6 row B label crop left edge shows the same yellow remnant as image 5
problems.root_cause: Matte artefacts inherited from source asset, not introduced by compose
problems.repair: Defringe/choke matte border in asset prep, keep as retained source defect otherwise

problems.problem: Contact shadow still a compact nub, not a graded occlusion
problems.evidence: Image 6 row B contact crop: dark bump under base, no lateral falloff on cloth
problems.root_cause: Shadow model limited to contact dab
problems.repair: Add wide low-opacity ambient occlusion ellipse consistent with diffuse frontal light

problems.problem: Over-bright green base plus slight label skew combine
problems.evidence: Image 6 row C contact crop green band neon-bright; row C label crop top edge tilts
problems.root_cause: Linear-light trim missing plus residual placement rotation
problems.repair: Tone-trim transmissive green and reset placement rotation

problems.problem: Weakest contact occlusion of the set
problems.evidence: Image 6 row C contact crop: contact nub faintest, cloth barely darkened under base
problems.root_cause: Shadow opacity under-set in linear pass
problems.repair: Increase occlusion alpha and radius to match diffuse frontal lighting

reason: B keeps the bottle, cap, label and glass transmission closest to the packshot source (fidelity 97), shows the cleanest silhouette edges of the four, matches the scene's diffuse frontal light without inventing a hard beam, and has the strongest actual contact occlusion in the authoritative detail row. A and C introduce a neon-green base and label skew; baseline carries the weakest edges. No version clears the >=88/all-clear acceptance bar because the source matte remnants and nub-style contact shadow persist everywhere, so B is preferred as the best-controlled integration rather than an approved final.

next_repairs.action: Choke/defringe 1-2 px to remove yellow blob and neck jaggies while preserving true glass transmission
Replace contact nub with a graded elliptical occlusion matched to diffuse frontal light; keep density at or above baseline
Add display-referred trim after linear-light compose to tame the transmissive green base; zero the residual label rotation
Verify label horizontals against canvas after re-placement to lock the straightest label of the set
